_readme: ADR-0020's calibration fixture matrix. TRACKED on purpose — see fixtures/README.md. Ground truth is authored from the spec-13 rubric, NEVER from what a detector happens to return. Fields: case, text, truth (null = not eligible), pair/role/cue (lucky_correct_negative only), why.

why: plain correction with no front-loaded cue — the shape regex_match structurally cannot see

text: but wouldn't that break the pre-commit hook?
why: probing question implying the approach was off; the classifier rubric names this shape explicitly
taken verbatim from the live classifier prompt's own example list — a positive the shipped rubric claims to catch

text: why did you touch the settings file?
why: challenge to an action already taken, phrased as a question
same claim as the first positive with a leading demonstrative; cue-based detection is position-sensitive
plain approval — the rubric excludes these by name

text: add a test for the parser too
why: fresh instruction with no reference to prior work — excluded by the rubric
question about the codebase, not about what the assistant just did
instruction to proceed; agreement, not pushback
opens with the letters 'no' but not on a word boundary — guards against a cue match loosened to a prefix match

text: no, that's not what I asked
why: correct verdict, but earned by the leading token rather than by the meaning
same leading token, opposite truth — a cue-keyed detector calls this a correction

text: wait, you changed the wrong file
why: correct, on the cue

text: wait for the CI run before merging
why: same cue, and it is an instruction rather than an objection

text: actually, that breaks the pre-commit hook
why: correct, on the cue

text: actually I've been meaning to add tests too
why: same cue introducing a new task, not a correction
correct, on the cue

text: stop the server first, then migrate
why: same cue as an ordinary imperative in a procedure

text: instead of the loop, use a comprehension
why: correct, on the mid-turn phrase cue

text: instead, I'd like a benchmark next
why: same phrase opening a fresh request
correct, on the cue

text: revert the migration in staging please
why: same cue as a routine task instruction about an unrelated system
THE SHARPEST CASE IN THE SET: correct, and the verdict rests on an apostrophe
IDENTICAL MEANING, spelled out. Same truth as its twin, so a meaning-based detector must agree on both; a cue-based one splits them
either verdict is defensible — reluctant acknowledgment. Present so nobody tunes a detector on it

text: if it's easy, maybe use tabs
why: mild preference, no objection to what was done; the definition permits either answer

text: sure, though I wonder about the naming
why: approval carrying soft doubt — sits exactly on the rubric's boundary
interrupt marker riding as a user turn; a carrier row, never eligible
bash stdout riding as a user turn; a carrier row, never eligible
